origin: From the Bauhaus, the art and architecture school that opened in Weimar, Germany, in 1919. The German name means building a house, and it put function and basic shapes before ornament.
whenToUse: Posters for exhibitions or cultural events.
Covers that combine shapes and letters.
whenNotToUse: Shapes would cover the letters and make them hard to read.
Primary colors don't fit the brand.
accessibility: Check that large styled text still contrasts with its background.
Screen readers should hear the same phrase as is, not the decorated letters.
The phrase keeps its meaning even with the decorative effect removed.
A toggle to compare with plain text shows the difference the effect makes.
